title: Challenge: The Dicee Challenge
section: 17. Boss Level Challenge 1 - The Dicee Game
summary: Introduces the first boss-level project: a two-player dice page that rolls random dice on every refresh and announces the winner. Starter HTML/CSS is supplied so the focus stays on DOM and JavaScript, with an option to rebuild the HTML/CSS from scratch.

concepts.heading: What the finished page does
points: An h1 headline reads 'Refresh Me' on first load.
Below it are two dice panels labelled Player 1 and Player 2, each with a dice image.
Every page refresh rolls two random values, swaps both images to match, and replaces the headline with the result (which player wins, or a draw).
Purpose of the project: apply the DOM, selection, attribute and text manipulation skills from the previous section in a standalone build.

concepts.heading: How to approach it
points: Use the provided starter project (next lecture) with HTML and CSS done, so only JS needs writing.
Optional extra practice: ignore the starter markup, open the finished Dicee page in Chrome from the skeleton zip and recreate the HTML and CSS to match. The zip includes the dice image assets.
Recommended practice is to concentrate on one new skill at a time, which is why the skeleton is provided.

task.name: Dicee Game
task.starting_point: Skeleton project with index.html, styles.css and the dice images (dice1.png to dice6.png), with both players showing dice 6 initially.
task.goal: On every refresh, roll two random dice, show the matching images, and announce the winner in the h1.
steps: Download the skeleton and open it.
Add an external JavaScript file and link it (steps follow in the next articles).
Generate two random numbers from 1 to 6.
Update both img elements to the matching dice image.
Change the h1 text to show Player 1 wins, Player 2 wins, or Draw.
task.expected_result: Refreshing the page shows two random dice and a headline naming the winner or a draw.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 17 - Boss Level Challenge 1 - The Dicee Game

pitfalls: Reference repo adds emoji flags and a personal footer, which are not part of the lesson.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (no s17.js data file).
gaps_and_ideas: New project lesson: 'Dicee: random dice game'. Blurb: build a two-player dice roller with DOM updates.
Tasks: (1) link script.js, (2) get two random 1-6 numbers, (3) set both img src values, (4) show a winner in the h1, (5) stretch: add a roll button without reloading.
Starter: Dicee HTML/CSS with images; use inline SVG dice or emoji faces if images are unavailable.
Demo: rolled-number histogram over 600 rolls to show Math.random is roughly uniform.
